hint.text: The picture shows a banana plant with dozens of bananas hanging closely together. This is called a banana cluster. At the end of the banana cluster is a huge flower.

atoms.text: Bananas are long, slightly curved, edible fruits which grow in big clusters on banana plants. Bananas grow in more than 135 countries around the world. Both their sweet taste and peel, which conveniently offers natural protection and an organic packaging material, makes bananas the perfect snack.

Bananas change their colour over time. After initially turning from green to yellow, they eventually begin to turn brown and become sweeter as they continue to ripen. The combination of sweet taste and organic packaging makes bananas one of the most popular fruits in the world.

hint.text: This picture shows plantains at a market in Costa Rica.

atoms.text: Plantains are very similar to bananas, in shape and colour. As with bananas, plantains also have their own protective peel. As a matter of fact, in many parts of the world, there is no strict distinction between bananas and plantains. In some places one word describes both, while in other places, each fruit has their own name.

Bananas are referred to as sweeter and softer, while plantains are described as a firmer and bigger fruit. The main difference, however, is that plantains are often eaten cooked, whereas bananas are generally eaten raw. Plantains can be used for cooking at any stage of ripeness, even if the peel is still green.
